beats.beat: The company's product portfolio spans four categories: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM). These are specialty chemicals used across industries.
Sales are routed through the network of its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, under a long-term arrangement. This means the company's revenue is tied to the promoter's distribution strength.
Customer concentration is high: the top 10 customers accounted for around 59% of revenue from operations in each of FY2015, FY2016, and FY2017.
Exports reached Rs 1,068.18 lakh over the past five years, with destinations including Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka.

The company cites six competitive strengths: a diversified product portfolio, diversified user industries, import substitution potential, support from its holding company, product innovation via R&D, and a strong management team.

beats.beat: Profit after tax (PAT) turned around from losses in FY2013 (Rs 27.40 lakh) and FY2014 (Rs 12.17 lakh) to modest profits in subsequent years. PAT stood at Rs 149.58 lakh in FY2015, declined to Rs 90.18 lakh in FY2016, then rose to Rs 174.82 lakh in FY2017. For the six months ended September 2017, PAT was Rs 132.75 lakh.
Basic earnings per share (EPS) improved from negative to positive: (0.45) in FY2013, 2.47 in FY2015, 1.46 in FY2016, 2.43 in FY2017, and 1.48 for the six months to September 2017.

Cash flow from operations has been volatile. It was Rs 200.97 lakh in FY2013, Rs 127.73 lakh in FY2014, jumped to Rs 422.36 lakh in FY2015 and Rs 802.59 lakh in FY2016, then turned sharply negative at Rs 349.75 lakh in FY2017. The six-month period to September 2017 showed a positive Rs 124.86 lakh.
Total assets have been relatively stable: Rs 3,018.66 lakh in FY2013, declining to Rs 2,592.53 lakh in FY2015, then rising to Rs 3,424.96 lakh by September 2017.
Revenue from operations is not disclosed in the extracted facts, preventing a margin or growth analysis.

beats.beat: The company is closely held. Promoters — Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited — hold 89,48,270 equity shares, or 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up capital. Promoter group (excluding promoters) holds the remaining 0.24%.
Related-party transactions have occurred over the last five financial years and the six months ended September 2017, as detailed in the financial statements (page 223 of the DRHP).

Governance flags include: (i) past instances of non-filing, incorrect filings, or delays with the Registrar of Companies; (ii) lack of certain statutory licenses for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia; (iii) the company does not own the premises for two manufacturing facilities and two administrative offices; and (iv) the corporate logo is not registered.
The company, promoters, group company, and directors are involved in certain legal proceedings, the outcome of which could be material.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals segment (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) is valued at about Rs 1,000 billion as of FY2017, having grown at 10–12% CAGR from FY2014 to FY2017. CRISIL Research forecasts a 12–14% CAGR going forward.
The industry is highly fragmented, with small and medium enterprises holding 70–75% market share. Global players also compete, and only a few Indian firms have the scale to match them on innovation.

Growth is driven by increased consumption, a growing middle class, urbanisation, government policy support (Draft National Chemical Policy, 100% FDI), and favourable global factors such as China's stricter environmental regulations reducing its specialty chemical output.
Specific sub-segments have strong growth projections: construction chemicals and water chemicals at 15% CAGR, polymer additives at 10%, textile chemicals at 12%, and surfactants at 13%.
A headwind: India's chemicals industry has consistently imported more than it exported over 2012–2017, with imports growing at a slightly faster CAGR (6.4% vs 6% for exports).

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals — a mix of functional additives, chemically modified minerals, and unmodified soft and hard minerals. It relies on its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products. The company is raising money through a fresh issue of equity shares to fund a new manufacturing facility and for general corporate purposes, and plans to list on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE).

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of equity shares to be listed on the SME Platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE). The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

Proceeds will be used to fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and for general corporate purposes. Listing will also create a public market for the company's shares.
The DRHP does not disclose the issue size, price band, or offer-for-sale component (if any). The selling shareholder is also not named.

beats.beat: Reliance on short-term purchase orders: The company has no long-term agreements with customers or raw-material suppliers. Volume and pricing are governed by individual purchase orders, making revenue and costs unpredictable.

Negative operating cash flow in FY2017: Cash from operations turned deeply negative at Rs 349.75 lakh in FY2017, after being positive in prior years. Sustained negative cash flows could constrain growth and servicing of debt.

Missing statutory licenses: The company has not yet obtained all required licenses for its manufacturing facility at Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia. It could face penalties or operational disruptions if non-compliance is enforced.

Intense competition and pricing pressure: The specialty chemicals industry is fragmented with many SME players. Competition could force price reductions, squeezing margins and affecting profitability.

Related-party transactions: The company has a history of related-party transactions and may continue them. There is no assurance that these will not adversely affect financial condition or that they are conducted at arm's length.
